unified_features.name: Unified sign-in (password and OAuth)
unified_features.rationale: Password accounts (A) and federated sign-in (B) are two ways into one identity; the user wants one account per person, so both methods write to one user store and issue one kind of session.
unified_features.behaviour: register_password creates a user (role editor, mapped from A's user) owning the normalised email; login_password and login_oauth both return a session token; login_oauth finds the (provider, subject) identity, else joins the user that owns the email only when email_verified is true, else creates a separate user (role viewer, mapped from B's member); whoami resolves a live token to user_id, email and current role; logout revokes the token; tokens expire.
unified_features.improvements: A: duplicate email rejected instead of overwritten; constant-time hash comparison; one AuthError for every sign-in failure; sessions expire and can be revoked. B: email_verified decides linking; an unverified email never takes ownership of an address; sessions issued (B had none).

unified_features.name: Role-based permissions
unified_features.rationale: Only Roster has a permission model; it becomes the one role set for every account, with A's and B's role names mapped onto it.
unified_features.behaviour: Roles viewer (read), editor (read, write), admin (read, write, manage_roles); one can(role, permission) check that denies unknown roles; map_source_role maps A user -> editor, B member -> viewer, C roles unchanged, and raises KeyError for anything else.

unified_features.name: Admin role management
unified_features.rationale: Roster's admin-only role change, kept as its own feature on top of the unified permissions and sessions.
unified_features.behaviour: set_role(token, user_id, role): the caller is resolved from the session; PermissionError unless the caller has manage_roles; the role must be a unified role; nobody can raise their own role; bootstrap_admin creates the first admin once, during setup.
unified_features.improvements: The actor comes from a verified session instead of a caller-supplied role; the new role is validated; raising your own role is refused; first admin created by an explicit setup step.
